To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) AAMs based on flash calcination of metakaolin, GGBS and FA are promising alternatives to Portland cement 2) Blended AAMs (based on two precursors) have the potential to improve some of the main properties of pure AAMs 3) The use of a ternary representation to study AAMs is a useful tool for the optimization of the formulation and the characterization of these materials

(1) the use of a ternary representation to design AAM mixes is a useful approach; (2) the use of two precursors is an interesting way to optimize the performances of AAMs; and (3) the association of MK and/or GGBS is an efficient way to optimize shrinkage mass loss and compressive strength.
the use of a ternary diagram to represent AAM compositions and to study their properties is a very useful tool to optimize the properties of AAMs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and optimization of blended AAMs.
the production of AAMs with good performances in the fresh and hardened states.
the formulation and characterization of blended AAMs based on flash calcination metakaolin, FA and GGBS and the influence of activator amount on the properties of these AAMs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
blended AAMs have the potential to become a viable alternative to OPC.
the use of a blended AAM (FA MK GGBS) is a promising solution for reducing shrinkage and mass losses in AAMs and for improving their mechanical performances.
the association of two precursors is an interesting approach to improve the performance of AAMs in terms of shrinkage and early compressive strength.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AAMs based on MK and GGBSS can be successfully used as a replacement for OPC in building applications.
blended AAMs can be considered a good alternative to OPC in the production of concrete.
the use of two precursors is an efficient way to improve the performances of the resulting AAMs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of blended AAMs could lead to significant improvements compared to pure AAMs.
the use of a blend of precursors can lead to the production of an AAM with better properties than a pure one.
the combination of MK and GBBs can lead to a reduction of the main drawbacks of AAMs, shrinkage and high mass loss, without affecting compressive strength.
